This is an explicitly reduced boundary problem from the original 64² Kbasement=1e-3 case. It retains the full geometry/gradient stencils and makes only 196 heads free (a 7×7 square through four layers). Every exterior unknown is prescribed the independently polished GPU Picard head. Contacts outside the free patch are removed. Original sources on newly fixed cells remain recorded as reservoir data and are excluded from the free-cell budget. This is not the original full-domain boundary problem.

The two saved roots are verified diagnostic seeds, not cold-start benchmarks. The test perturbs both and independently resolves the CPU equations; both conserve with a head separation of about 0.377 m. They demonstrate a reproducible nonlinear branch issue without selecting a physically preferred root. Full provenance: validation_artifacts/terrain_2026-10-16/cpu_branch_reductions/terrain_64_k0.001/radius_3.
